newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called higher in line with OTC.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called higher in line with OTC.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures are called to open higher Wednesday in line with higher over-the-counter (OTC) prices after Tuesday's gains on shortcovering and keen buying interest in the physical market.
"We're seeing another strong rise," said a West Coast electricity dealer.

In OTC activity, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $14.25-14.60 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Tuesday's settle at $14.15, while June Palo Verde at $19.35-19.65 compared with yesterday's close at $18.85.
"Right now, people just want to see how high they could take it," said a New York futures broker.
Spot electricity supply in the Northwest remains tight as Bonneville Power Administration would likely continue offering limited amount of next-day power.
Canada's B.C. Hydro pulled out of exporting surplus power to the U.S. as reservoir levels at the Arrow Dam in British Columbia approach flood control limits.
A 550 megawatt (MW) unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming is expected to stay down until tomorrow after being taken offline last week for repairs.
The power complex may receive another boost from stronger natural gas futures, market sources said.
The June Henry Hub natgas contracts opened up 0.8 cent at $2.150 per million British thermal units.
Forecasters said the Northwest would see a break from clouds and rain Thursday and Friday, but some areas would cool considerably over the next couple of days.

By Friday, temperatures would average four to six degrees F below normal in the western region and 10 to 16 degrees F below in the eastern region. Readings would moderate toward near normal levels by Sunday.

In the Southwest, temperatures in the northern and eastern sections would run eight to 12 degrees F below normal through Friday, while readings in the southern area would average two to four degrees above normal.
